answer: Interleaved Arrival Spacing Gate. Each identity must start activity in a slot drawn from a publicly logged schedule, and the round-trip lag between its first two messages is checked against a quartz oscillator baseline. Traffic shaped like a mesa—flat, simultaneous bursts—is rejected, since honest agents arrive staggered. The rule enforces a minimum spacing canyon between first-contact times across any cluster of new identities. An attacker pays by running many parallel clients through a delay line, adding real latency and coordination overhead per identity.
